thread:
maria: FYI customer (ACME Corp) opened a P1 — internal API hostname `api.acme.internal.redwood` intermittently NXDOMAIN from their prod VPCs. They see 5xx and high latency when requests hit our public LB fallback. Can we triage?

jon: Got it. Which VPCs exactly? Any pattern (region/account)?

maria: Two VPCs in us-east-1 (acct 123456789012): prod-app and prod-batch. Prod-app resolves fine from their dev VPC, but prod-app VPCs get NXDOMAIN. Happens since ~08:30 UTC.

sophie: Quick check — can you paste the dig/nslookup from an affected instance? Need to see which resolver returns NXDOMAIN.

maria: Paste from customer:
```
$ dig @10.0.2.2 api.acme.internal A +short
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
$ dig @10.0.0.2 api.acme.internal +short
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
;; flags: qr aa rd; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0\n```
They also ran `dig @8.8.8.8 api.acme.internal +short` -> NXDOMAIN (expected). From a working dev VPC: `dig @10.0.2.2 api.acme.internal +short` -> 10.5.6.7

jon: That smells like split-horizon: a private hosted zone exists but not associated with the affected VPCs, or there is a resolver rule forwarding to the wrong place.

alex: Agree. Common causes: (1) Private Route53 hosted zone not associated with VPC, (2) overlapping zones in another account with higher priority resolver rule, (3) custom DHCP / custom DNS server in the VPC returning NXDOMAIN, (4) Route53 Resolver outbound endpoints missing for cross-account resolution.

maria: Customer says they recently migrated some subnets and updated VPC peering. Could be VPC associations got dropped.

sophie: Can they run these quick checks from an affected instance and paste results?
- `cat /etc/resolv.conf`
- `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name "acme.internal" --query HostedZones[*].Id`
- `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id <id> --query VPCs`
- `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules`

maria: They ran `cat /etc/resolv.conf`:
```
nameserver 10.0.2.2
search ec2.internal
options timeout:2 attempts:2
```

kevin: `10.0.2.2` looks like the VPC resolver. Good. If the resolver returns NXDOMAIN for private zone it means the private zone either isn't associated with that VPC or a higher priority rule/forwarder is responding.

maria: They ran the hosted zone check in the account we expect, and the hosted zone exists but the `get-hosted-zone` output shows only dev VPC listed. prod-app and prod-batch not present.

jon: There we go. Not associated. How did that happen? Maybe change in IaC removed the association during migration.

sophie: Two fix options: (A) Associate the private hosted zone with the missing VPCs (fast), (B) add a Route53 Resolver rule + outbound endpoint if it's cross-account and you don't want to associate. Prefer A for same-account VPCs.

maria: Customer tried to associate but gets `InvalidVPCId.NotFound` error for prod-batch when using Console API; prod-app association succeeded. They suspect the VPC CIDR changed earlier in a refactor.

alex: If the VPC ID not found error occurs, confirm that the association attempt uses the correct account/region. Also check if the VPC was recreated (new ID).

maria: They confirmed the VPC was recreated (new ID) during the subnet refactor. The IaC team didn't re-run the hosted zone association for the new VPC.

sophie: OK action plan:
1) Re-associate the private hosted zone to the new VPC IDs (`aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id ZZZZZ --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=vpc-0abcd1234`).
2) If cross-account, create a Route53 Resolver inbound/outbound endpoint or share the zone with RAM.
3) Verify resolution with `dig @<vpc-resolver> api.acme.internal +short` and `curl --resolve api.acme.internal:443:10.5.6.7 https://api.acme.internal/health` to ensure TLS cert covers the name.

maria: Customer performed associate on prod-app and it worked. prod-batch needed the new VPC id; once they used the new id association worked. After association `dig @10.0.2.2 api.acme.internal +short` -> 10.5.6.7.

kevin: Great. One more note: if customers have egress allowlists (corporate proxies), make sure the VPC resolver traffic is allowed — internal resolution to private zones must reach the Route53 resolver locally. Also check security groups if using resolver endpoints.

maria: They did have a temporary firewall rule blocking outbound DNS to the VPC resolver from a sample instance — that explained the earlier `connection timed out` from one dig run. They removed that.

triage-bot: Escalation created: INC-2026-ACME-DNS (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026). Assigned to sophie and jon.

sophie: I'll add a postmortem checklist: audit IaC that recreates VPCs to ensure hosted zone associations are part of the deployment, add a CI/GH action test that verifies internal hostnames resolve from a newly created VPC.

jon: Also recommend adding an alert in Console when a private hosted zone loses expected VPC associations (CloudWatch event + Lambda that compares desired associations).

maria: Customer confirms service is healthy after associations and firewall fix. They want follow-up on IaC checklist. I'll close the P1 once sophie posts the remediation ticket. :thumbsup:

alex: Marking root cause: hosted zone not associated to recreated VPC + transient firewall rule blocked DNS. Two independent failures that combined to produce the outage.

maria: Thanks team — will loop back with the customer on next steps and attach the dig outputs and commands used.

kevin: Nice writeup, please add the `associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone` CLI snippet and the docs link to the incident ticket: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/hosted-zones-private.html

maria: Will do. Closing thread after postmortem is filed.
